description: Actual original-series Pokémon anime battle music plus staged Poké Ball flight and opening/creature-emergence cues.
reproduce: python3 scripts/prepare-battle-audio-v13.py. Requires only Python 3, curl, ffmpeg and ffprobe. Optional ASSET_FFMPEG, ASSET_FFPROBE and REVEAL_AUDIO_SOURCE_CACHE. All sources are SHA-256 pinned; output is limited to public/assets/audio-v13.
encoder: ffmpeg version 8.1.2 Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers
formats: Stereo MP3 192 kbps / 44.1 kHz and OGG Opus 128 kbps / 48 kHz. Decoded duration, not container duration including codec delay, defines the browser AudioBuffer timeline.
validation: All six files decode with ffmpeg -xerror to finite PCM; decoded durations within 3 ms; 4x oversampled peaks within 0.3 dB of target. Effects begin below -55 dBFS and end below -65 dBFS. Music wrap waveform step is compared with nearby normal sample steps. Per-file timings, levels and SHA-256 hashes are recorded.
limitations: Automated technical validation only; no listening review is claimed. Source game effects can be low-rate original assets; output resampling does not create detail. Swish Foley is Kenney CC0; Pokémon music/game recordings follow the user's stated license, with mirror provenance recorded separately.

flight.intent: A distant, soft approach grows into a close airy throw as the Poké Ball reaches the card. Start once at flight launch, not at contact.

sources.rights: Copyrighted Pokémon GO sound, reused under the user's stated Pokémon license. PokeMiners is a community asset archive; no open-license claim is made.

layers.purpose: Authentic game throw reversed and stretched without repitching for a soft distant approach
Quiet recorded swish supplies airy detail as the ball gets close
Original-pitch game throw crests at about 0.935 seconds and decays into contact

processing.method: 48 kHz stereo float mixing of source excerpts; normalized ingredient peaks before relative balance; source-specific EQ and fades; final DC removal and 20 ms silent codec guard. No oscillator tones, generated noise, artificial reverb or master limiting. Original pitch retained in every layer; only the distant flight layers are reversed/time-stretched as documented.

release.intent: Immediate authentic Poké Ball opening burst, followed by a low airy expansion and a restrained sparkle under the creature entrance. Start at shell opening; keep the species cry separately scheduled.

processing.selectionEvidence: A repeated musical passage near 14.296 / 83.836 seconds was identified by three-second chroma similarity of 0.885 at a 69.54-second lag. Fine waveform correlation refined the lag to 69.549 seconds. This is numerical phrase matching, not an audition claim.
processing.method: Original stereo recording with gentle 35 Hz high-pass / 14 kHz low-pass. A 240 ms complementary sine-squared circular crossfade joins matching musical passages. No silence, tempo/pitch change, extra instruments, vocals or generated music added. Each codec is independently normalized using decoded four-times-oversampled peak measurements.

backgroundMusic.playback: Decode to an AudioBuffer, loop the full 69.549-second decoded buffer, fade its bus in over 0.45 seconds and out over 0.65 seconds. Start only when a pack opens. Duck to about .16 during ball effects and creature cries, returning smoothly to .34 afterward. Avoid an HTML media-element loop when exact gapless timing is required.
backgroundMusic.limitations: The source is a community MP3 rather than a verified lossless master. Track identity, phrase similarity, duration, waveform continuity and headroom were checked; no human listening or musical-seam audition is claimed.
